cropProtectionSegment.title: Crop Protection segment
cropProtectionSegment.content:
The Crop Protection segment -- herbicides, fungicides, insecticides, biologicals, nitrogen management and seed-applied technologies -- is reported alongside segment adjusted EBITDA (before corporate costs and the Vylor transition agreements).

For Corteva, Inc.: since the 2026-10-01 spin-off of the Seed/genetics business to Vylor Inc. (VYLR), this segment is effectively the whole continuing company. Segment EBITDA margin ran 16.6-19.9% over FY2021-25 before sliding toward the mid-teens in 2026 as a severe Brazil channel destock and generic price erosion on mature molecules hit volumes and pricing together.

What to watch:

  • Whether the 2026 margin compression is a trough (management's 2027 case) or the new normal
  • Progress on the $130-140m manufacturing-network restructuring (through 2028)
  • Latin America volumes as the clearest swing factor quarter to quarter

cropProtectionMix.title: Crop protection product mix
cropProtectionMix.content:
Revenue split across the four core chemistry families: herbicides (~45% of sales), fungicides (~15%), insecticides (~10%) and biologicals (~5%); the remainder is seed-applied technologies, nitrogen management and other lines not broken out here.

For Corteva, Inc.: patent-protected new actives (Zorvec in fungicides, Arylex and Enlist-compatible chemistries in herbicides) are growing and carry premium pricing, but they are still a minority of a mix dominated by older, off-patent molecules facing intensifying Chinese, Indian and UPL-style generic competition. Biologicals is the smallest line and the only one with a stated long-term target (~$1bn annualized revenue by decade-end), yet it fell YoY in 2026 on Brazil volumes alongside everything else.

What to watch:

  • Herbicide pricing on mature, off-patent molecules (e.g. North America acetochlor)
  • Fungicide weakness concentrated in Latin America versus the Zorvec growth story
  • Biologicals re-accelerating toward its long-term target once Brazil stabilizes

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Corteva, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Corteva, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Corteva, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Corteva, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Corteva, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Corteva, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Corteva, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Corteva, Inc.: this series still carries the combined pre-spin company (Seed + Crop Protection) through the periods reported before the 2026-10-01 Vylor separation -- it is not the standalone Crop Protection entity the DCF values. See the Crop Protection segment chart below for the continuing business on its own.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Corteva, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
